China announces countermeasures amid US rare earth and trade disputes

China's Commerce Ministry announced countermeasures against the U.S. following U.S. trade sanctions. These measures include suspending factory follow-up inspections by Chinese certification bodies, blacklisting U.S. compliance testing companies, and launching national security investigations into imports of office printers and copiers. This action occurs amidst broader discussions about U.S. efforts to reduce reliance on China for critical minerals, particularly rare earths used in weapons manufacturing, and concerns about China's advancements in areas like sixth-generation aircraft programs.
